title: Grease and flour a Nordic Ware 6-cup Bundt pan: coat every flute and turn out the loose flour
instruction: Grease and flour the Bundt pan for baking: no bare spots, no loose flour left in it. Leave it upright on the sheet pan.
context: Home bakers grease and flour cake pans before filling them so the cake releases intact; missed creases can tear a cake and excess flour leaves a chalky crust. On this reusable Nordic Ware 51202 Bundt pan, the brush must reach the outer flutes, rounded floor and centre tube. Flour adheres to the shortening; turning the pan over sheds the loose powder while retaining the release coat. This is the maker's pan-preparation method, completed without baking a cake.
setup: Kitchen counter (the station table). Positions are centres in cm: forward from the line through the two arm bases, left of their midpoint. Lot A (the screenshot): (1) Nordic Ware Naturals aluminium half sheet pan (43100), 45.4 x 32.8 x 2.5 cm, centred at (36, 0), long side across the robot. (2) On it, a Nordic Ware Original Bundt pan, 6-cup (51202), cast aluminium with a silver non-stick inside, 20.6 cm across the body, 23.5 cm across its two handles, 8.3 cm tall, 0.55 kg (estimate), centred at (33, 0), empty, clean and dry, handles to the left and right. Its inside: 12 rounded flutes about 6 mm deep that run down the outer wall, across the rounded floor and up the centre tube (3.2 cm across at the top, with a 2.5 cm bore through it). (3) On the sheet pan at (25, -18), a 4 oz white porcelain ramekin (8.9 cm across, 4.4 cm tall) holding 2.5 cm (about 120 g) of Crisco All-Vegetable Shortening at room temperature (about 21 C), levelled. (4) On the counter at (34, -40), a white ceramic spoon rest, 20 x 7 cm, with a raised pad 2.2 cm high under the lower end of the brush's handle and a notch 4.2 cm high near its far end; a Nordic Ware natural-bristle pastry brush (02122), 20.3 cm long, 3.8 cm wide head, 91 g, lies on it pointing away from the robot, rising 14 degrees toward its handle, bristle tips at (44, -40) just clear of the counter. (5) On the counter at (30, 31.5), a Tablecraft 159 stainless flour dredger (7.1 cm across, 9.4 cm tall) holding 25 g of all-purpose flour (Gold Medal). Lot B: the ramekin at (25, 18), the spoon rest and brush at (34, 40) and the dredger at (30, -31.5); everything else as lot A. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Real trials: cover gripper fingers, pads and finger roots with removable snug nitrile covers; keep seams above the contact pads and replace torn covers. Fit removable wrist sleeves and a washable catch cloth beneath the full working area, including the brush rest and dredger. Keep the half sheet and all object positions as listed; collect flour outside it from the cloth as counter spill. Use commercially supplied shelf-stable shortening and dry flour; the reusable empty pan is the specimen.
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial if the cake pan's downward speed ever exceeds 0.6 m/s, or object/arm state is unreadable. A 20 fps real-trial video uses more than 30 mm downward travel between frames as the drop check. Score 0 unless the final pan is upright within 10 degrees, its feet within 4 mm of the sheet pan floor and its centre inside the sheet pan walls; brush and dredger bounding boxes do not overlap the pan's; both hands are at least 30 mm clear of its body and handles; pan speed is at most 5 mm/s and 0.05 rad/s for 1 s. Then the assessor photographs each of 12 flutes' outer wall (rim to 46 mm deep), floor (below 46 mm) and tube (46 mm deep to tube top), 36 zones, with a ruler. A zone fails for a connected bare patch at least 10 mm long. Turn the pan over a tared tray, tap its rim three times on the tray edge and weigh the loose flour with a 0.01 g scale. With Z zones passing: 1.0 if Z=36, loose flour <=0.5 g, no deposit >2 mm and counter flour <=2 g; 0.75 if Z=36 and loose <=2 g; 0.5 if Z>=24 and loose <=2 g; 0.25 if Z>=12; otherwise 0. Loose flour >2 g, a deposit >2 mm (feeler gauge), or counter flour >2 g caps the score at 0.25. Collect and weigh counter flour outside the half sheet. The simulation reads its declared coating field and recorded poses; photographs, gauges and collected masses are the proposed real-trial checks. Average the scores of lots A and B.
reset_notes: Use the commercial empty pan repeatedly with shelf-stable shortening and dry flour; no cake, fresh food specimen, curing or baking is needed. Budget 5-8 minutes for wash, dry and reset (planning estimate). Wash the pan and brush in warm water with mild detergent and a soft nylon brush; rinse and towel-dry the flutes, tube, brush and handles fully. Swap in an identical clean, dry pan and brush if drying delays the next trial. Remove and discard finger covers without spilling their powder; replace covers and clean removable wrist sleeves. Collect flour outside the half sheet for scoring before cleaning the catch cloth, sheet pan and tools. Set the pan back with handles left/right and the brush tips away on its rest. Level shortening to 25 mm at about 21 C; refill the dredger to 25.00 g. Check every flute and the tube is dry and free of visible residue, the brush is clean/dry, covers are intact, and all positions match lot A or B before starting. Lot B mirrors only the ramekin, brush/rest and dredger positions given in setup. Real-trial kit and budget are listed in the README.
fidelity: Isaac Sim rigid pan, brush and dredger at product scale; flute profile estimated. Shortening/flour use 4,992 surface cells with geometric bristle overlap, not measured contact force. Bristles/ferrule have no collider or bending. Flour adheres only to greased cells; loose powder slides above 45 degrees; inverted dredger releases 0.8 g/s. Tapping, powder dynamics and material forces are unmodelled; rates are estimates. Recorded demo/model scores are simulation results.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0; step limit); demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0)
